alt.en: The top of an old printed page in two columns inside a ruled frame, headed "The Taming of the Shrew." and numbered 221. Near the top of the left column a speech marked "Gru." reads "Oh I Curtis I, and therefore fire, fire, cast on no water." Lower in the same column another reads "Why Iacke boy, ho boy, and as much newes as wilt thou." The right column is dialogue among servants.
alt.es: La parte de arriba de una página impresa antigua a dos columnas dentro de un marco de líneas, con el encabezado "The Taming of the Shrew." y el número 221. Cerca del principio de la columna izquierda, un parlamento marcado "Gru." dice "Oh I Curtis I, and therefore fire, fire, cast on no water." Más abajo, en la misma columna, otro dice "Why Iacke boy, ho boy, and as much newes as wilt thou." La columna derecha es un diálogo entre criados.

caption.en: Page 221 of The Taming of the Shrew in Shakespeare's collected plays of 1623: Grumio's "therefore fire, fire, cast on no water" turns the round's cry upside down, and his "Why Iacke boy, ho boy" a note of 1788 calls the start of another old round.
caption.es: La página 221 de La fierecilla domada (The Taming of the Shrew) en las obras reunidas de Shakespeare de 1623: el "therefore fire, fire, cast on no water" de Grumio le da la vuelta al grito del canon, y de su "Why Iacke boy, ho boy" una nota de 1788 dice que es el comienzo de otro viejo canon.

source: William Shakespeare, Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies (London: Isaac Jaggard and Ed. Blount, 1623), The Taming of the Shrew, p. 221, top of the page cropped; scan page n236
library: Internet Archive (Early English Books microfilm collection)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1623; Shakespeare died 1616, editors John Heminges 1630 and Henry Condell 1627, printers Isaac Jaggard 1627 and Edward Blount 1632. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed page of old notes headed "OBSERVATIONS." and numbered 133, with "Vol. III. T of the Shrew." in the margin. Note 476, "fire, fire; cast on no water.", reads "There is an old popular catch of three parts, in these words:" and quotes three lines, "Scotland burneth, Scotland burneth. Fire, fire; Fire, fire; Cast on some more water.", signed "E." Other notes, several signed "Malone", are above and below it.
alt.es: Una página impresa de notas antiguas con el encabezado "OBSERVATIONS." y el número 133, con "Vol. III. T of the Shrew." en el margen. La nota 476, "fire, fire; cast on no water.", dice "There is an old popular catch of three parts, in these words:" y cita tres versos, "Scotland burneth, Scotland burneth. Fire, fire; Fire, fire; Cast on some more water.", firmada "E." Arriba y abajo hay otras notas, varias firmadas "Malone".

caption.en: Page 133 of the 1780 supplement to Johnson and Steevens's Shakespeare: a note signed only "E." explains Grumio's "fire, fire; cast on no water" by quoting "an old popular catch of three parts" that begins "Scotland burneth".
caption.es: La página 133 del suplemento de 1780 a la edición de Shakespeare de Johnson y Steevens: una nota firmada solo "E." explica el "fire, fire; cast on no water" de Grumio citando "un viejo catch popular a tres voces" que empieza "Scotland burneth" (Escocia arde).

source: Supplement to the Edition of Shakspeare's Plays Published in 1778 by Samuel Johnson and George Steevens, vol. 1 (London, 1780), p. 133, note to vol. III, p. 476; scan page n164
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1780; editor Edmond Malone died 1812, George Steevens 1800; the note's writer, signed "E.", wrote in 1780 and so died long before 1926. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: A stained, yellowed book page numbered 21. At the top, the last two verses of a song, ending "To celebrate ancient St. John." Below a double rule is "SCOTLAND'S BURNING! CANON.": four numbered lines of notes in 3/4 with the words "Scotland's burning, Scotland's burning," "Look out, Look out," "Fire! Fire!" and "Cast on". The right half of the last two lines is lost to a pale damaged patch.
alt.es: Una página de libro amarillenta y manchada, numerada 21. Arriba, las dos últimas estrofas de una canción, que terminan "To celebrate ancient St. John." Bajo una doble raya está "SCOTLAND'S BURNING! CANON.": cuatro líneas numeradas de notas en 3/4 con las palabras "Scotland's burning, Scotland's burning," "Look out, Look out," "Fire! Fire!" y "Cast on". La mitad derecha de las dos últimas líneas se ha perdido en una mancha pálida dañada.

caption.en: Page 21 of David Vinton's The Masonick Minstrel (Dedham, Massachusetts, 1816): "Scotland's Burning! Canon.", the earliest printing with music we found, its last line partly lost to damage in this copy.
caption.es: La página 21 de The Masonick Minstrel, de David Vinton (Dedham, Massachusetts, 1816): "Scotland's Burning! Canon.", la primera impresión con música que encontramos, con su última frase en parte perdida por los daños de este ejemplar.

source: David Vinton, The Masonick Minstrel (Dedham: printed by H. Mann and Co. for the author, 1816), p. 21, "Scotland's Burning! Canon."; scan page n26
library: Boston Public Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Boston Public Library HS453.V78; Internet Archive masonickminstrel00vint
licenceEvidence: Printed Dedham, Massachusetts, 1816; David Vinton died 1833 (library record: "Vinton, David, 1774-1833"). Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Boston Public Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A cream music page numbered 195, headed "LONDON'S BURNING". Four numbered lines of melody in 3/4 with one sharp: "London's burning, London's burning," "Fetch the engines, fetch the engines," "Fire! Fire! Fire! Fire!" with accents over three of them, and "Pour on water, pour on water." The line ends are numbered 4, 3, 2, 1, and "Back to beginning" is printed under the last.
alt.es: Una página de música color crema, numerada 195, con el encabezado "LONDON'S BURNING". Cuatro líneas numeradas de melodía en 3/4 con un sostenido: "London's burning, London's burning," "Fetch the engines, fetch the engines," "Fire! Fire! Fire! Fire!" con acentos sobre tres de ellos, y "Pour on water, pour on water." Los finales de línea llevan los números 4, 3, 2, 1, y bajo la última está impreso "Back to beginning".

caption.en: London's Burning on page 195 of the "Daily Express" Community Song Book (London, 1927), edited by John Goss: the earliest printing of "Fetch the engines" that we found, and the page our round is sung from, a tone lower.
caption.es: London's Burning en la página 195 del "Daily Express" Community Song Book (Londres, 1927), editado por John Goss: la primera impresión de "Fetch the engines" que encontramos, y la página de la que cantamos nuestro canon, un tono más abajo.

source: "Daily Express" Community Song Book, collected and edited by John Goss (London: The London Express Newspaper, 1927), p. 195, "London's Burning" (the other two rounds on the page cropped out); scan page n198
licenceEvidence: Published London 1927 ("Copyright, U.S.A. 1927, by John Goss"), so public domain in the US since 1 January 2023; editor John Goss died 1953, so life plus 70 ended 2023 in the UK, EU and Israel. Words and tune traditional, no other maker named on the crop. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
